defaultModel.rules:
Priority: a model picked inside a chat > these defaults > auto.
Model on Auto: new chats use the engine's default model. Effort on Auto: follows the model family's declared default.
"Restore auto" clears both defaults and returns to auto.

versionGuard.title: Stop old versions overwriting local files
versionGuard.desc: Local only: remembers a fingerprint of each Drive file's content. If sync ever writes back content this machine has already seen and which is not the newest (typically another device uploading an old copy), it restores the local shadow copy and tells you. A file you saved yourself in the last 15 seconds is never treated as a rollback. Off restores the plain Drive behaviour: no fingerprints, no shadow copies.

groups.noRoles: No roles yet. Add one, then pull it into a discussion from the sidebar's New meeting.
groups.noMembersYet: No speakers arranged yet. Tap a role below to add it; drag to reorder speaking order.
groups.hostHint: You are the host: you open with the topic, and the last member closes each round.
groups.roleOrderHint: Drag to set speaking order: earlier speaks first; the last member summarizes each round.
groups.summaryModeHint: After all rounds close, your session model writes the final minutes in this mode.
groups.changeDirectionPlaceholder: New direction for the next round; it is appended to the meeting's topic & rules with a timestamp (next round only)
groups.panelEmpty: No groups yet. Define roles and create a group in Settings → Groups.
groups.panelEmptyV2: No meetings yet. Click "New meeting" — it gets its own directory and topic & rules document.
groups.panelContinueDisabled: Nothing to continue yet — start a new session
groups.removeConfirmDesc: Only the meeting config is removed; its folder, document and chats stay on disk.
groups.createDesc: Name and roster first; the folder is created automatically, direction and materials are optional.
groups.createNameHint: Also the meeting folder name; submit is blocked while empty.
groups.createNameNoSlug: The meeting name needs at least one letter or number.
groups.createRosterLabel: Robots in the room (checked speak, drag to order)
groups.createNoRoles: No robots yet — create roles first.
groups.createFocusPlaceholder: e.g. gross-margin elasticity after subsidy taper, BNPL penetration focus
groups.createMaterialsEmpty: No materials is fine — folders can be added any time.
groups.createMaterialsHint: At start-up each folder is indexed by text file; members read on demand, nothing is bulk-loaded.
groups.createCollision: A meeting named "{{name}}" already exists — this joins its folder instead of creating a new one.
groups.roleInstructionPlaceholder: What this role is responsible for, which angle it takes, what its output must look like.
groups.fieldTopicPlaceholder: One question per discussion, e.g. What actually drove the balance down?
groups.roleModerator: Moderator (closes the discussion with the final plan)
groups.rolesDesc: A role is a set of instructions plus a model: who speaks in the group and from which angle. The instructions can be written here, point at a markdown file, or name a skill.
groups.roleExpandHint: Expand a role to edit its model, persona and skills; the name is editable inline.
groups.groupAutoDiscuss: Start the roster when I speak
groups.barPausedHint: Anything you send now is an interjection: answers already written stay, and the roster restarts from round 1 and runs to the end.
groups.barDone: Discussion finished · back to a normal chat
groups.defaultsDesc: The skeleton the summarizer uses to close each round; also sets how many cycles a new group starts with.
groups.summaryTemplateHint: The summarizer answers on this skeleton after each round; headings are kept verbatim. Takes effect from the next round.
groups.createFolderPending: Name the meeting first; it defaults to ~/Documents/ALWith/groups/.
groups.noMeetingSession: No named meeting subfolder or reusable conversation was found. Make sure the meeting folder exists, or pick it manually with "Choose a folder".
groups.documentHint: The meeting discusses around this document and its outputs follow it; every participant complies. Editable here — saving applies to all members.
groups.createDone: Created: the directory and topic & rules are ready. You can start in the main window; this dialog stays put — close it whenever you like.
groups.dialogHint: Drag the header to move · double-click it to reset · drag any edge or corner to resize

automation.schedulerHint: Runs automatically while the app is open — you don't need to keep this page open.
automation.pageDesc: Runs your prompt on a schedule and files every result under one monitoring conversation.
automation.completionSoundDesc: A rising two-note chime when a conversation finishes, and a different three-note cue when it needs your approval. Failures stay silent. System notifications and the Dock badge are unaffected.
automation.batchHint: Batch management is not available in this first version
automation.emptyHint: Click "New" in the top right to create your first task
automation.newDesc: Runs inside one monitor conversation named after the task; every result and summary accumulates there.
automation.sectionAdvancedHint: Only controls how results are delivered — it does not change how the task runs.
automation.larkAuthMissing: No signed-in Lark user found. Sending as the bot to meetings still works; sign in under Workbench → Extensions → Components if you want to send to yourself.
automation.fieldPromptPlaceholder: Describe what the agent should do, e.g. read a Feishu group and send a daily summary
automation.modelHint: Leave it on the default to use whatever a new chat starts with. Only models the engine and your providers currently serve are listed.
automation.larkBroadcastHint: On by default; turning it off means this task sends no result body.
automation.larkOffHint: On for new tasks — the result text goes to the authorized user. Turn it off if you do not need it.
automation.larkNoTarget: No recipient yet, so nothing will be sent. Pick a chat or a person to enable delivery.
automation.larkFormatHint: Plain text does not support rich text; bold, lists and links stay as literal characters.
automation.larkIdentityHint: Agent identity works out of the box; user identity needs the extra im:message.send_as_user scope. The two identities cannot be on together.
automation.larkUserPermissionHint: User identity needs Lark authorization. Turning it on checks the scope automatically; if it is missing, the authorization flow opens and can be closed at any time.
automation.larkUserPermissionDesc: Sending as yourself needs the im:message.send_as_user scope. Scan the QR code to authorize, or close this dialog and keep using the agent identity.
automation.larkUserPermissionExpired: The QR code expired. Refresh and try again.
automation.larkUserPermissionDesktopOnly: Lark authorization is only available in the desktop app.
automation.larkSelfSend: Send to me as the agent
automation.larkSelfSendHint: On by default; sends to {{name}} (signed-in user).
automation.runNoContent: No report body was produced in this run
automation.larkBotNote: The Lark CLI assistant sends as the app and needs no local QR authorization. Check Workbench → Extensions → Components if the app is not enabled in your org.
automation.larkNoGroups: No chats found — check that lark-cli is signed in
automation.larkHint: When on, the full result text of each run is posted to the targets below. Recipients come from your local lark-cli; the id is stored, so renaming a chat keeps the target.
automation.runsClearConfirmDesc: This deletes all {{total}} run record(s). This cannot be undone.
automation.runNeedsAuth: "{{name}}" is waiting for authorization — handle it in the main window
automation.runNowWaiting: Awaiting authorization — handle it in the main window
automation.larkCliMissing: The Lark CLI is not installed on this machine, so nothing can be sent. Install it, then reopen this dialog.

support.larkDesc: Installation, version and updates. Group-chat pushes run on the app identity, independent of sign-in.
support.nodeDesc: The runtime for lark-cli and the source of the npm package manager.
support.npmDesc: Ships with Node.js and is used to install and update lark-cli.
support.notLoggedInHint: You're not signed in with your Feishu account. Signing in only confirms your identity; to read docs and sheets, tick the permissions below afterwards. Group-chat pushes need no sign-in.
support.identityHelp: Permissions this account has. Tick any missing ones to request them.
support.scopeHelp: These are the scopes actually read from lark-cli. Tick missing ones and use the button below to generate an authorization QR code.
support.authSuccess: Signed in. To add permissions, tick them in the list below.
support.scanQr: This sign-in code only confirms your identity — it doesn't request extra permissions. Tick the permissions you need in the list below instead.
support.nodeInstallNote: Downloads the official installer package and opens the system installer; follow the prompts (admin password required).
support.nodeInstallStarted: Opened the Node.js installer — finish it, then click “Detect” to refresh.
support.nodeInstallFailed: Automatic install failed; download and install manually from the official site.
support.larkInstallNote: Downloads the platform binary from the npm mirror into the app's own folder — no admin rights needed.
support.larkUpdateSuccess: Lark CLI updated to {{version}}. Restart the app to use it.
support.larkUpdatedRestart: Updated to {{version}}. Restart the app to use the new version.
support.brewDesc: The macOS package manager that several components depend on; installing it requires an admin password in Terminal.
support.brewInstallNote: Runs the official install script in Terminal — enter your admin password in the popped-up Terminal, then click “Detect” to refresh.
support.accountDesc: Confirm your identity with your Feishu account; request extra permissions below. Group-chat pushes need no sign-in.
support.appNotConfiguredTitle: One more step: set up app credentials
support.appNotConfigured: Lark CLI is installed but no app is bound yet. Run the command below in a terminal once, follow the browser prompts, then click Recheck.
support.configCommandCopied: Command copied — paste it into a terminal
support.configCommandCopyFailed: Copy failed. Select the command above and copy it manually.
support.installFirst: Install Lark CLI first, then you can sign in.
support.scopesDialogHint: {{count}} selected. Scan the code to confirm.
support.allPermissionsReady: All required permissions are in place
support.qrExpired: This code has expired. Get a new one.
support.waitingForScan: Waiting for the scan — this finishes automatically, no button to press.
support.botNoApp: No app credentials configured yet; the bot identity isn't available.

errors.surfaceOperationInProgress: Another window operation is still running. Please try again.
errors.handoffStalled: The previous window operation did not respond. The interface is usable again — please retry.

enterprise.title: Enterprise sign in
enterprise.accountHint: This is your Finture enterprise account. Signing out here does not sign you out of ALwith U.
enterprise.error: Could not read or update enterprise authorization. Please retry.
enterprise.logoutHint: This stops conversations using enterprise models. Personal ALwith and custom models remain available.

providerUsage.title: Quota
providerUsage.consoleOnly: This provider's plan usage is only visible in its own console.
providerUsage.unsupported: This provider publishes no usage endpoint.
providerUsage.unsupportedDisabled: This provider is switched off, so no quota was read.
providerUsage.unsupportedNoBaseUrl: This provider has no API base URL, so there is nowhere to ask.
providerUsage.unauthorized: The key is invalid or has expired.
providerUsage.freeBlocked: Today's free calls are used up
